clue.text: Moocher, A-levels being dealt with — me escaping?

definitions.text: Moocher, A-levels being dealt with — me escaping?

indicators.note: letters that are being dealt with are shuffled like a hand of cards, so the clue's letters are rearranged
escaping says the two letters of the word me get away from the pool before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy teenager, exams finally over, imagines slipping away from it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being dealt with' rearranges MOOCHER plus ALEVELS, once 'me escaping' has taken M and E out of the pool. The whole clue also describes the answer: a loafer whose A-levels are done, off out of school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who has finished A-levels and is idling before what comes next is a youngster just out of secondary education.

clue.text: Garments — clown is wearing heaps

indicators.note: the heaps word is worn by the clown, so it wraps around it

parts.note: cocks are heaps, as in haycocks
an ass is a fool or clown

explanation.surface: Clothes worn by a clown in large quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wearing' means the heaps go round the clown like clothing. The heaps are haycocks, the conical piles of hay left in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassocks are long robes worn by clergy and choristers, a type of garment.

clue.text: Birds making shrieks in the East End?

indicators.note: in the East End of London speakers drop their aitches, so the initial letter goes

parts.note: howls are shrieks or loud cries

explanation.surface: Creatures that cry out in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney accent of London's East End drops the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey, famous for their hooting and screeching.

clue.text: Say, the girl is running much more than a few miles!

definitions.text: much more than a few miles!

indicators.note: running means moving about freely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The young woman is jogging well beyond an ordinary distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, nearly six trillion miles: a vast understatement.

clue.text: In an unnatural way, truly, the leader is replaced

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the truly word, and this says it is swapped for another

parts.note: verily is an old word for truly

explanation.surface: Something genuinely odd happens when a boss is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter changes: V becomes E. The clue does not name the incoming letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily means in a strange, uncanny or spooky manner, unnaturally.

clue.text: Plant, the thing right inside that display case

indicators.note: inside puts the thing and right within the plant

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
it means the thing

explanation.surface: Put the plant in the cabinet over there.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitrine is a glass cabinet for displaying objects such as china or curios.

clue.text: Protests as tormenters going free

indicators.note: going free means breaking loose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People object as their tormentors are released.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to protest forcefully, objecting or complaining.

clue.text: Holy oil in church is kept in small room

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the word is goes within the room

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Sacred oil in a church is stored in a little side room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small room' is the abbreviated room, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrism is consecrated oil used in anointing at baptism, confirmation and ordination.

clue.text: So controlled by violent husband

indicators.note: controlled by means held within the grip of the words violent husband, so the letters are tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A grim aside: so she was dominated by an abusive partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning 'in this way' or 'therefore', as in 'thus it was done'.

clue.text: Listened to record with a beat that comes from power?

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

indicators.note: listened to signals that what follows is taken by ear, so the spelling changes but the sound stays

parts.note: a rhythm is a beat in music

explanation.surface: Someone played a rhythmic record that seems to have a strong electric charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listened to' affects only the last piece: RHYTHM spoken aloud gives the written ending RITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the exponent, or power, to which a base must be raised to produce a given number.

clue.text: The writer getting guns up on revised agenda spuriously fixed?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me
gats are guns, in gangster slang

indicators.note: revised means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author with guns pushes a rigged programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MEGATS to STAGEM in this down clue; 'revised' turns AGENDA into ANAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stage-managed is orchestrated to look spontaneous, so arranged falsely or rigged.

clue.text: Stumbles, getting the lowest possible mark in exam

indicators.note: getting here means taking a letter into itself, so the stumbles word receives the zero inside it

parts.note: trips are stumbles
zero, written O, is the lowest mark one can score

explanation.surface: A student falters and scores nothing in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the honours exam at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the final honours examination for a Cambridge BA degree, a specific instance of an exam.

clue.text: Horse of great height buried in holy hill

indicators.note: buried in says one word is put deep inside another

parts.note: Sion, or Zion, is the holy hill of Jerusalem
tall means of great height

explanation.surface: A towering horse is found entombed in a sacred mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, so the answer is a kind of horse.

clue.text: Call boss, having secured opponents at table

indicators.note: having secured means holding fast inside, so the boss word encloses the opponents

parts.note: to dominate is to boss about
at a bridge table East and North are positions, abbreviated E and N, each opponents of the other pair

explanation.surface: Ring the boss, who has seated rivals around a table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; any one of East and North opposes a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: To denominate is to name or designate something, and to call something is to name it.

clue.text: Guarding amenities is such an estate worker

parts.note: the four letters spanning the end of Guarding and the start of amenities are a field-sport word for hunted animals, and those words keep it, holding it inside

explanation.surface: The person minding the facilities on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: 'Guarding amenities' keeps GAME hidden within it (guardinG AMEnities), so the phrase is literally a keeper of GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper is employed on a country estate to rear and protect birds and animals for shooting.

clue.text: Fellow seen as dope given boot ultimately

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the very last letter of the word boot

explanation.surface: A man regarded as an idiot is finally kicked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gent is short for gentleman, an informal word for a man or chap.

clue.text: A member of family crosses valley on farmland maybe

indicators.note: crosses here means spans over, so the relative word goes around the valley

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, a member of the family
a ria is a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A relative travels across a valley to some fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to cultivated land and agriculture, so it could describe something on farmland.

clue.text: Island's mess

definitions.meaning: A small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
... is dirt or a mess, as in '... up'

explanation.surface: The island is in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names a small Hebridean island; the other is filth or a muddle, both meanings of the same word.

clue.text: Features like The Archers on the radio? They are corny

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the spelling is ignored

parts.note: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera, an example of a serial

explanation.surface: A comment that radio soaps are hackneyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC Radio 4 soap about farming life.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals are grains such as wheat, oats and maize, literally corn crops; corny jokingly means made of corn.

clue.text: Gosh, with death invading capital, there's a catalogue of errors!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: invading means pushing into, so the death word goes inside the capital

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
end means death, as in 'came to a sticky end'

explanation.surface: An exclamation as death sweeps into a city, followed by a list of blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' sends death into the Latvian capital. 'Cor' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda is a list of mistakes in a printed book with their corrections, a catalogue of errors.

clue.text: Sweet nothing — hard to become leading character

indicators.note: to become says one letter changes into another

parts.note: nought means nothing, zero
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
A is the leading character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Sweet nothings get harder until one plays the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet nothing' looks like one phrase; 'Sweet' is the definition and 'nothing' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Nothing wrong in gambling game, almost a sport

indicators.note: in puts the nothing and wrong letters inside the game
almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bingo is a gambling game of numbers
O is the figure zero, nothing
X is the mark for a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Nothing wrong with a betting game: it's nearly sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BINGO to BING, and OX goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing is a combat sport fought with fists in a ring.

clue.text: Drug problem managed the wrong way by firm — crisis, not half

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the six letters of crisis is dropped

explanation.surface: A company crisis over drugs is badly mishandled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns RAN into NAR; 'not half' removes CRI from CRISIS, leaving SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a stupor or unconsciousness induced by drugs, a medical problem caused by a narcotic.

clue.text: Formal greeting — it comes with an instrument

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A ceremonial welcome accompanied by music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention from the 1920s phrase 'she has it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of respect or welcome, often in military or ceremonial settings.

clue.text: Island gets heat unit with temperature dropping

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a therm is a unit of heat used for gas billing

explanation.surface: An island gets its heating as the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is one of the Channel Islands, near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Herm is a small island in the Channel Islands group, between Guernsey and Sark.

clue.text: Film-maker taking backward step in serious move

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: grave means serious

indicators.note: taking a backward step means going in reverse, so the name is read from the end

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director (Monsieur Hulot's Holiday)

explanation.surface: A director retreats as part of a solemn manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking backward step' reverses the surname of Jacques Tati, the French director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday; 'in' places it inside the word for serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to move or be drawn towards something, as by gravity.

clue.text: Lake disappearing from Scottish island? Fancy that!

indicators.note: disappearing from means the letter vanishes out of the island name

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: A loch vanishes from a Hebridean isle, prompting astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; 'I say!' is a dated British expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Hellish situation before a welcome with chaps in altercation

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the hellish realm

indicators.note: in puts the chaps inside the welcome word

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A dreadful scene before an arrival leads to a row involving some men.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel, a heated falling-out between people.
